title: Support Worker - Children & Young People's Services
description:
Support Worker - Children & Young People's Services

Newcastle upon Tyne
13.00 - 20.00 per hour
Zero Hour Contract

Pin Point Health & Social Care is recruiting experienced Support Workers to work across a variety of Children's Residential Homes, Supported Accommodation Services, and Young People's Settings throughout Newcastle and the surrounding areas.

This is an ideal opportunity for individuals who are passionate about making a positive difference and enjoy working across a range of services supporting children and young people with varying needs. We're looking for proactive, engaging, and reliable staff who can quickly build positive relationships and adapt to different environments.

The young people you support may have experienced trauma, emotional and behavioural difficulties (EBD), learning disabilities, mental health needs, or complex family backgrounds. Your role will be to provide practical and emotional support while helping them achieve positive outcomes and reach their full potential.

The Role
- Supporting children and young people with daily routines, activities, education, and independence skills.
- Building positive relationships and acting as a positive role model.
- Encouraging engagement in education, hobbies, and community activities.
- Providing emotional support and promoting positive wellbeing.
- Managing challenging behaviours in a calm and professional manner.
- Maintaining accurate records and safeguarding documentation.
- Working across a variety of children's and young people's services as required.
- Promoting safeguarding and welfare at all times.

What We're Looking For
- Minimum 6 months' experience supporting children and young people.
- Experience within residential care, supported accommodation, education, or similar settings.
- A proactive and engaging approach to supporting young people.
- Strong understanding of safeguarding and professional boundaries.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Flexibility to work across different services.
- Full UK driving licence preferred.

Why Join Pin Point Health & Social Care?
- Competitive hourly rates and weekly pay.
- Flexible shifts to suit your availability.
- Opportunities across a variety of services.
- Regular ongoing work available.
- Dedicated consultant support.
- Training and development opportunities.

If you're passionate about supporting children and young people and want a varied role working across multiple services, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today.

title: Female Enabling Support Worker
description:
Female Enabling Support Worker

Location: Newcastle

Salary: £13.45 per hour

Hours: 40 hours per week

Are you the Enabling Support Worker We're Looking For?

Do you have a passion for supporting people with complex needs to live fulfilling, independent lives? Are you an experienced care professional ready to take the next step in your career?

At Shaftesbury North East, we're looking for dedicated and motivated Enabling Support Workers to join our Complex Care Service. We are looking for someone with a sense of fun, to help make a real difference to the lives of the people we support every day. Knowledge of the local area would be advantageous.

Due to service requirements, only Female applicants will be considered. A full UK license is required. Please note that we are not currently offering Sponsorship for this role.

About You

To be successful in this role, you'll have:
- A minimum of 12 months' experience supporting people with complex needs, learning disabilities, autism, and behaviours of concern within a supported living environment.
- NVQ/QCF level 2 or a desire to work towards the qualification while working
- A person-centred approach and a genuine passion for delivering outstanding support.

About the Role

As a Enabling Support Worker it will be your role to provide support and encouragement, by taking direction from both the person supported and the person centred support plan.

You will be required to maintain accurate records while at work, in line with the service requirements. You may also be required to administer personal care and medication.

There may be a requirement to cover sleep in sessions. You will be paid an additional £60 per sleep in.

Benefits of working at Shaftesbury

At Shaftesbury, we know that our workers are our greatest asset. We're proud to have some of the best and most committed staff in the sector - and we want to attract more people like you to work with Shaftesbury. We're now offering even more great benefits to reward the work of our wonderful staff, which is listed below:
- Happy Birthday to you! As well as sending you a birthday card, all frontline care staff can have the opportunity to take the day off on their birthday, taken from your annual entitlement.
- Great CQC, great reward. If your service is rated good or equivalent by CQC in all domains, all staff will receive a £30 gift voucher. If rated outstanding, all staff will receive a £50 gift voucher.
- We want to reward staff in a range of ways for their hard work. You can be nominated for a recognition letter from a member of the Executive Leadership Team and you may also be nominated to receive a gift voucher up to £50 for going above and beyond within your role.
- Excellent training package provided for all staff.
- Generous Annual Leave entitlement of 25 days + 8 days bank holiday for the first 5 years. Increasing to 28 days + 8 days bank holiday after 5 years.
- Pension Scheme.
- Access to our employee assistance program.

Shaftesbury is the disability charity that's committed to enabling children, young people and adults to live a life that adds up for them.

What makes life liveable is never down to just one thing - it's the sum of many things. From friendship to fun; from companionship to community; from a great chat to a challenge overcome, it all adds up - to Shaftesbury.

Through a wide range of disability care, special education, and rehabilitation services we promote inclusion and wellbeing for all. Together, we work to see people take part, contribute and be valued. We put the elements in place that all add up to connected lives.

Shaftesbury is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable children and adults and expects all employees to share this commitment. All offers of employment are subject to an enhanced DBS/Access NI check.

Shaftesbury is committed to the Disability Confident Scheme and to equal opportunities therefore we welcome and encourage applications from everyone regardless of age, disability, gender, ethnicity, religion and sexual orientation.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Shaftesbury Group, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

title: Health Care Assistant
company: Atlas Care Homes Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Reports To

Senior Carer / Clinical Lead / Home Manager

Location

Job Purpose

To provide high-quality, person-centred care and support to residents, promoting their independence, dignity, privacy, choice, and well-being at all times. The Healthcare Assistant will work closely with nurses, senior carers, and the wider care team to ensure residents receive compassionate and professional care in accordance with individual care plans and company policies.

Key Responsibilities

Personal Care
- Assist residents with personal care activities, including bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and oral hygiene.
- Support residents with eating and drinking, ensuring nutritional and hydration needs are met.
- Maintain residents' dignity, privacy, and independence during all aspects of care.

Mobility and Support
- Assist residents with mobility, transfers, and repositioning using approved moving and handling techniques and equipment.
- Support residents to participate in social, recreational, and therapeutic activities.
- Monitor residents' well-being and promptly report any changes in physical or mental health to senior staff.

Care Delivery
- Follow individual care plans and risk assessments.
- Assist with daily living activities and provide emotional support to residents and their families where appropriate.
- Support senior carers and management in delivering safe, effective, and person-centred care.
- Maintain accurate and timely care records in accordance with company policies and regulatory requirements.

Health and Safety
- Comply with all Health & Safety, Infection Prevention and Control, Safeguarding, and Medication policies.
- Report accidents, incidents, hazards, concerns, or safeguarding issues immediately.
- Ensure a clean, safe, and comfortable environment for residents.

Person Specification

Essential Criteria
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Compassionate, caring, and patient-centred approach.
- Ability to follow instructions and work effectively within established care procedures.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Flexible approach to working hours, including weekends and bank holidays.
- Understanding of dignity, respect, confidentiality, and safeguarding principles.

Desirable Criteria
- NVQ/QCF Level 2 or Level 3 in Health and Social Care.
- Previous experience working within a residential care home, nursing home, or healthcare setting.
- Training in Moving and Handling, Safeguarding, Infection Control, and First Aid.
- Experience supporting elderly residents and those living with dementia.

Please note: Sponsorship is not available for this role. Applicants must already hold the legal right to work in the United Kingdom.

title: Domiciliary Care Worker
description:
Job Title: Domiciliary Support Workers
Location: Newcastle
Start Date: Immediate Start
Salary: £15.50 - £17.00 per hour

Are you an experienced Domiciliary Support Worker with a passion for supporting autistic adults and individuals with complex needs?

Do you have experience supporting individuals in residential homes and implementing positive behavioural support approaches?

Are you a compassionate and proactive individual who can lead by example and promote high standards of person-centred care?

TeacherActive is proud to be working with a specialist care provider based in Newcastle, who are looking to appoint dedicated Domiciliary Support Workers. The setting provides person-centred support to autistic adults and individuals with complex needs within their residential homes, promoting independence, dignity and meaningful opportunities while maintaining high standards of care.

The provider is looking to take on experienced Domiciliary Support Workers on a full-time, long-term basis, with the opportunity to become permanent for the right candidates. The successful Domiciliary Support Workers will provide support within residential homes, assist with daily living activities, promote independence and implement positive behavioural support strategies, while supporting the Team Leader with supervisory responsibilities, modelling best practice and participating in senior on-call duties when required.

The successful Domiciliary Support Workers will have:
- A relevant health and social care qualification or a willingness to work towards one
- Experience supporting autistic adults and individuals with complex needs, with a strong understanding of positive behavioural support approaches
- Previous experience supervising a team, promoting best practice and maintaining high standards of care
- Excellent verbal, written, IT and interpersonal skills, with a willingness to develop knowledge of Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements
- A compassionate, mature and proactive approach, with the flexibility and physical fitness to participate in agreed activities and support service delivery
- The ability to deputise for the Team Leader and participate in senior on-call duties, with a full, clean UK driving licence advantageous but not essential

In return for the above you can expect to receive:

- The opportunity to secure a permanent position, with benefits including annual leave, sick pay, life insurance, a pension scheme and career progression opportunities

Our staff are paid on a PAYE basis, so you can rest assured that you re paying the right level of TAX and National Insurance and there s no messing around with admin charges coming out of your hard earned cash.

description:
Job Title: Care Assistants

Location: South Shields, South Tyneside

Salary: 14.44 - 14.94 per hour + 35p per mile for driving roles

Job Type: Permanent - Full Time, Part Time or Casual (guaranteed hours available)

No care experience? No problem. We'll give you full paid training, two paid shadow shifts and a fully funded Social Care diploma, so all you need to bring is a passion for helping others.

About us:

North Haven Care and Support Ltd is a Good CQC rated home care provider across South Tyneside and Sunderland. We help people with a wide range of conditions stay independent, stay in control of their own lives and stay in the homes they love.

About the role:

As a Care Assistant, you'll visit clients in their own homes and out in the local community, helping them live well and keeping their pride and dignity. No two days are the same. You'll help with:
- Personal care
- Preparing meals
- Administering medicine
- Shopping and household tasks

We have a number of positions available and are recruiting for two types of role:
- Driving carers (3-4 roles): you'll need a full licence and access to a vehicle, with mileage paid at 35p per mile
- Walking carers (2-3 roles): no licence needed, as you'll cover clients within walking distance of each other

Shifts: Earlies (7am-3pm) and/or lates (3pm-11pm) on a rota, with some weekends. Choose the hours that fit around childcare, study or other commitments.

Areas covered: Marsden, Whitburn, Cleadon, The Nook, Simonside, West Harton, Brockley Whins, Westoe, West Park and Tyne Dock.

About you:
- You're caring, compassionate and a good listener
- You enjoy building relationships with a diverse range of individuals
- You can drive and have access to a vehicle (preferred)
- Experience is welcome but not required. Experienced carers with an up-to-date DBS check can start quickly

What we offer:
- Up to 14.94 per hour, plus 35p per mile for driving roles
- 28 days' annual leave (pro rata)
- Paid classroom training and paid shadow shifts
- Fully funded QCF diploma in Social Care and a clear route to progress
- Flexible hours and guaranteed hours contracts
- Pension scheme
- Free on-site parking
- Referral programme

Additional Information:

All successful candidates will need an enhanced DBS check.

If this sounds like the ideal opportunity for you just click on the APPLY button, we look forward to hearing from you!

Candidates with experience of; Care Assistant, Carer, Home Carer, Care Worker, Domiciliary Care Worker, Domiciliary Carer, Support Worker, Community Care Worker, Healthcare Assistant, Personal Care Assistant, Home Care Assistant, Social Care Worker will also be considered for this role.

title: Children Support Worker
description:
Residential Support Worker - Make a Real Difference Every Day

Are you passionate about supporting children and young people to achieve positive outcomes? Do you want a rewarding career where you can make a genuine difference in a child's life?

We are recruiting on behalf of a specialist residential childcare provider for a Residential Support Worker to join a dedicated team in Sunderland. This is an excellent opportunity for caring, resilient and motivated individuals looking to develop a career within residential childcare, children's services, support work, youth work or social care.

Whether you already have experience working with children and young people or are looking to take the next step into the sector, we'd love to hear from you.

The Role

As a Residential Support Worker, you will provide high-quality care and support to children and young people living in a residential home setting. You will help create a safe, stable and nurturing environment while promoting independence, personal growth and emotional wellbeing.

Key Responsibilities
- Supporting children and young people with daily routines, education and activities
- Building positive, trusting and professional relationships
- Encouraging independence, confidence and essential life skills
- Promoting emotional wellbeing and positive behaviour
- Creating a safe, caring and supportive home environment
- Working collaboratively with colleagues, families, social workers and external agencies
- Following safeguarding policies, procedures and children's care plans
- Maintaining accurate records, reports and documentation
- Supporting young people to achieve personal goals and outcomes

About You

We are looking for individuals who are:
- Caring, compassionate and committed to making a difference
- Resilient and able to remain calm in challenging situations
- Strong communicators with excellent interpersonal skills
- Reliable, professional and able to work effectively as part of a team
- Flexible to work shifts, weekends and sleep-ins
- Passionate about supporting vulnerable children and young people

Desired Experience

A relevant qualification in Health & Social Care, Children & Young People's Workforce or Residential Childcare is desirable but not essential.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive pay of £13.50 per hour
- Comprehensive induction and ongoing training
- Career development and progression opportunities
- Supportive and experienced management team
- Rewarding work with real purpose and impact
- Opportunity to build a long-term career within children's residential care

Apply Today

If you're looking for a rewarding Residential Support Worker job in Sunderland, and want to help children and young people thrive in a safe and supportive environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now for immediate consideration and take the next step in your residential childcare career.

title: Care Assistant - Care Home
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Care Assistant at Barchester, you'll play a vital role in helping our residents enjoy each day to the fullest. Providing both practical support and meaningful companionship, you'll make a genuine difference to the lives of the people you care for.

In this role, you'll:
- Support residents with daily living activities and personal care
- Help residents with food and drink throughout the day
- Build positive relationships and provide companionship
- Follow individual care plans and support resident wellbeing
- Spend valuable one-to-one time with residents
- Encourage independence while promoting dignity and respect
- Work as part of a caring team to deliver high-quality support

No two days are ever the same, making this a rewarding opportunity to use your skills, develop your experience and make a real impact every day.

ABOUT YOU

We're looking for someone who is kind, compassionate and committed to delivering excellent care.

To join us as a Care Assistant, you'll have:
- Experience caring for older people
- A positive, can-do attitude
- Excellent communication and people skills
- A warm, empathetic and respectful approach
- A genuine passion for supporting others

Above all, you'll have the compassion and dedication needed to provide the highest standard of care and support. In return, we'll give you all the training and development you need to succeed.

REWARDS PACKAGE

In return for your dedication, you'll receive a competitive rate of pay plus a sector-leading benefits and rewards package, including:
- Free training and development opportunities
- Access to wellbeing and support tools
- A range of retail discounts and savings
- Unlimited referrals through our Refer a Friend bonus scheme
- Employee of the Month recognition
- Long Service Awards
- Career development opportunities within one of the UK's leading care providers

And so much more!

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality of care you'd expect for your own loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

Our Care Home Manager is always happy to welcome you into the home for an informal chat, so feel free to pop in and find out more about working at Barchester.

title: Care Assistant
description:
Job Title: Care Assistant
Contract Type: Permanent
Salary: £26,227.50 per annum (pro rata)
Working Hours: 16 per week
Working Pattern: Saturday and Sunday only, one week earlies one week lates
Location: Willow Brook, Washington

If you share our values and are excited about making a significant impact at Riverside, please ensure you attach a current CV and covering letter. At Riverside we recruit to potential not just on skills and experience, so we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the essential criteria on the job description.

Please note that whilst we will accept applications on the basis of any form of valid legal permission to work in the UK, we will be surrendering the Riverside Sponsorship licence, so for the avoidance of doubt, we are unable to apply for any further sponsorships whether on behalf of existing colleagues or candidates.

The difference you will make as a Care Assistant

You will provide assistance to residents in need of physical personal care and carry out individual tasks with residents in line with their support plans, to maintain or improve their quality of life and to be able to recognise signs of distress in residents. You will work with the team to identify and assess positive ways to reduce distress and give residents control over their lives wherever possible.

About you

We are looking for someone with:
- Experience of working in a customer focused, residential environment, offering personal care to a diverse group of people
- An awareness of housing and Health and Safety legislation and regulation National Care Standards Awareness
- Flexibility to work hours to meet customer and business needs, which may include working outside of normal office hours and lone working

Why Riverside?

At Riverside, we're a housing association with a difference - enhancing the everyday for all our customers. For 90 years, we've been revitalising neighbourhoods and supporting communities by providing the homes they need to live full, fulfilling and rewarding lives.

We have a portfolio of over 75,000 affordable residential and retirement homes across the UK. Our work ranges from homelessness services to social care, employment support to retirement living, and we need the best people on board to help us.

Working with us, you'll enjoy:
- Competitive pay & generous pension
- 25 days holidays plus bank holidays (pro rata)
- Investment in your learning, personal development and technology
- A wide range of benefits

Diversity and Inclusion at Riverside:

We are inclusive. At Riverside, we value diversity in all its forms. We foster a workplace where all individuals are respected, empowered, and heard. Our commitment to inclusivity drives our success and enriches the lives of our customers and colleagues.

Riverside is a Disability Confident Employer and operates a Guaranteed Interview Scheme for any applicant who declares they have a disability. If the applicant meets the minimum requirements for the role (as set out in the role profile and/or person specification) they will be guaranteed an interview.

Applications may close before the deadline, so please apply early to be considered.

Role Profile
- Work as part of a committed and compassionate team, delivering an outstanding experience to customers whilst being supported by your colleagues and Line Manager.
- Recognise and identify each individual customer's needs to ensure a person-centered approach and that the customer is at the heart of everything we do by:
- Delivering and enabling customers to meet the aspirations within their individual support plans, whilst keeping up-to-date information on customers' changing needs.
- Providing direct personal care to customers in line with Care Quality Commission (CQC) definitions including showering, shaving, toileting, continence management and personal hygiene (training provided).
- Helping customers to go to bed, wake up, dress and maintain their personal appearance.
- Safely helping with customer's mobility difficulties and using assessed equipment, aids or other manual handling equipment.
- Administering and supporting medication for customers.
- Assisting with preparation of meals, snacks and drinks where necessary.
- Working with customers to provide light general household domestic duties, for example - cleaning, laundry, ironing, etc.
- Helping customers with the management of their personal affairs when this is part of their individual support plan e.g. reading letters, managing utilities, handling small amounts of money for shopping.
- Communicate clearly, building trusted relationships with customers and their wider support network (family, friends, GPs, Social Worker, etc.).
- Provide companionship to customers, engaging in conversation to build genuine and trusted relationships.
- Encourage customers to participate in social activities and feel part of the community.
- Ensure customers are safe at all times by carrying out all of your duties within Riverside's Policy and Procedure framework e.g. health & safety, equal opportunities, cash handling, etc.
- Take pride and initiative in working with customers to meet their needs, creating a safe, comfortable and respectful living environment.
- Maintain detailed, accurate records of care and medication support provided, as well as tasks undertaken.
- Promptly respond to and report any concerns relating to the care, support, well-being or behaviour of customers to a manager, making comprehensive records, ensuring customer confidentiality is observed at all times.

title: Support Worker Young People
description:
We are looking for a number of suitably experienced support workers for ad hoc shifts in young persons supported accommodation across Durham and surrounding areas.

You will be supporting in varying sized settings, all based around supporting young people transitioning out of care services and with a mix of complex needs, including mental health and substance misuse support needs. You will need to be experienced in working with young people and/or young adults, supporting them to develop life skills, assisting them to maintain tenancies, signposting and supporting them to find work or further education, helping them to develop budgeting and household management skills and any other appropriate support.

There are both day and night shifts available, and this would suit those seeking flexibility in their working patterns.

Working for Nurse Plus you will receive weekly pay and free industry leading training, with opportunities for ongoing development. You will have access to support from a local team, the flexibility to choose when to work and the chance experience a variety of exciting roles.

title: Young People's Support Worker
description:
Young People's Support Worker

Morpeth, Northumberland
15.00 - 22.00 per hour
Zero Hour Contract

Pin Point Health & Social Care is recruiting experienced Young People's Support Workers to support young people aged 10-17 years within a residential children's home in Morpeth.

This is a highly proactive and engaging role, ideal for someone who enjoys building positive relationships, getting involved in activities, and making a genuine difference to a young person's life. We're looking for staff who bring energy, enthusiasm, and resilience to every shift and are committed to helping young people achieve positive outcomes.

The service supports young people with emotional and behavioural difficulties (EBD) and behaviours that can be challenging. You'll be part of a dedicated team providing a safe, structured, and nurturing environment where young people can develop confidence, independence, and life skills.

One of the best things about this service is the range of activities available. From climbing frames and outdoor activities to indoor sports and games, you'll be encouraged to actively engage with the young people and help create positive experiences throughout your shift. This is a genuinely rewarding opportunity for someone who wants to have a lasting impact on a young person's life.

The Role
- Supporting young people aged 10-17 with their daily routines, activities, education, and personal development.
- Building positive relationships and acting as a trusted role model.
- Encouraging participation in sports, activities, and community opportunities.
- Supporting young people to manage emotions and behaviours positively.
- Promoting independence, confidence, and life skills.
- Maintaining accurate records and safeguarding standards.
- Working closely with the wider care team to deliver high-quality support.

What We're Looking For
- Minimum 6 months' experience within a children's residential setting.
- Experience supporting young people with challenging behaviours.
- A proactive, energetic, and engaging approach.
- Strong understanding of safeguarding and child-centred care.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- A full UK driving licence is desirable.

Why Join Pin Point Health & Social Care?
- Competitive rates of 15.00 - 22.00 per hour.
- Weekly pay.
- Flexible shifts to suit your availability.
- Ongoing opportunities within children's residential services.
- Dedicated consultant support.
- A rewarding role where you can genuinely make a difference.

If you're the type of person who likes to get involved, build positive relationships, and create positive experiences for young people every day, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today.

title: Regional Care Assistant
description:
A 500 'Golden Hello' Welcome Bonus is just one of the ways we'll reward you when you join Barchester in this role.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Regional Care Assistant with Barchester care homes, you'll deliver warm, empathetic and respectful care and support across a 20-mile radius to help our residents get the most out of life. On a practical level, you can expect to monitor the delivery of care when on duty, contribute to the person-centred care planning process for each resident and record observations on things like temperature and blood pressure amongst a range of other important tasks. The role of Regional Care Assistant is very varied and also involves providing support and companionship. It's vital for us that every resident enjoys meaningful one-to-one time with our carers, every single shift.

ABOUT YOU
A background in care is important for the role of Regional Care Assistant, and you'll need a good understanding of elderly care. A Level 2 NVQ in Health & Social Care would be useful, as would a good understanding of the wider healthcare industry. Ideally, you'll also have a C or above in GCSE English and Maths. Dedicated and compassionate, your passion for people means you'll go above and beyond to support the wellbeing of residents. Because you'll be travelling across the area, you'll either need your own car or ready access to one. We'll cover your mileage when you travel over five miles from your main home, and if you're on duty at the time of an inspection and we achieve a Good' rating, you'll qualify for a bonus.

Free training and development for all roles

title: Support Worker
description:
Helping others improve and turn their lives around - there's no better feeling. It's what we do for thousands of people at more than 150 sites across the UK. Be a part of it.

We are looking for confident Support Workers with a passion for delivering outstanding care.

You'll be working 42 hours a week (days/nights/alternate weekends), making a positive difference to the lives of the people in our care at Hope House.

Hope House is a residential service providing outcome focused care for adults with a learning disability and associated complex needs who may have behaviours that challenge.

We encourage and enable the individuals we support to lead a full and happy life. We work with them to ensure they have more choice and control in their lives. We find out their strengths, abilities and preferences so that the care provided can be as person-centred and meaningful to each individual as possible.

At Cygnet, our perks go way beyond pension schemes and excellent professional development.

You'll also enjoy shopping, travel and leisure discounts - as well as a range of healthcare and financial benefits - to support you to be happy both in and out of work.

Apply now to enjoy excellent career prospects while reaping the rewards of making a difference to others - every day.

Your day-to-day
- Offer enhanced care with a flexible learning approach for all the people in our care
- Provide guidance & encouragement through physical & emotional support
- Learn about individuals' specific needs & provide help in the most appr
opriate way
- Assist with medical & welfare needs
- Report on medical & welfare needs as required
- Safeguard
- Maintain a safe, clean environment for all

Why Cygnet? We'll offer you
- 13.15 per hour increasing to £13.45 per hour at 3 months and £13.70 per hour at 18 months
- Flexible working with opportunity for overtime
- Regular coaching & appraisal
- Expert supervision & peer support
- Employee discount savings & Cycle to Work scheme
- 24 hours free GP helpline
- Discounted Gym membership
- Free eye tests
- On site benefits including free meals
- Plus much more

You are
- Genuinely driven with a desire to make a real difference in people's lives
- An excellent communicator & a good team player
- Sensitive & intuitive with the energy required to provide a trusting, stimulating & varied environment
- Passionate about empowering & supporting service user independence

Successful candidates will be required to undergo an enhanced DBS check.

Cygnet has been providing a national network of high-quality specialist mental health services for more than 30 years. In this role you'll have the chance to make a real impact on patients, service users & their families.

title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Healthcare Assistants Drivers Essential Must be available for last minute shifts & Weekend work Care Home & Nursing Home work

Location: Northumberland, North East England
Company: Tyne Trust Healthcare
Job Type: Full-Time / Part-Time / Flexible Agency Work
Salary: Competitive Hourly Rates Weekly Pay

Experienced Healthcare Assistants Wanted Drivers Essential!

Tyne Trust Healthcare, an established healthcare recruitment agency based in Newcastle upon Tyne, is recruiting experienced, reliable and flexible Healthcare Assistants (HCAs) to support residential and nursing care homes throughout the North East.

We are looking for dedicated individuals who can provide high-quality care, respond to last-minute shift requests, and offer weekend availability.

This position is particularly suited to experienced Healthcare Assistants who enjoy flexible agency work, can adapt to different care environments and are willing to travel to support care homes when staffing needs arise.

Essential Requirements Please Read Before Applying

Applicants MUST meet ALL of the following criteria:
- Minimum 6 months' paid care experience within the last 18 months, in UK residential or nursing care homes.
- Full UK driving licence and access to your own reliable vehicle.
- Willingness to travel up to 1.5 hours each way from Newcastle upon Tyne to attend shifts.
- Availability for last-minute shifts, including requests at short notice and, where possible, on the same day.
- Weekend availability is essential, including the ability to work Saturdays and/or Sundays.
- Enhanced DBS clearance appropriate for working with vulnerable adults, or willingness to undergo the required checks.
- Good knowledge of safeguarding, moving and handling, infection prevention and control, and person-centred care.
- Excellent communication skills, professionalism and a compassionate attitude.
- Ability to work confidently and independently within different care home environments.
- A strong commitment to punctuality, reliability and maintaining high standards of care.
- Legal right to work in the UK.

IMPORTANT: This role requires flexibility, weekend availability, access to your own transport and the ability to respond to urgent staffing requests. Applicants unable to meet these requirements should not apply.

Key Responsibilities
- Deliver high-quality, person-centred care to residents in nursing and residential care homes.
- Assist with personal care, dressing, washing and daily living activities.
- Support residents with mobility, transfers and moving and handling.
- Assist with nutrition, hydration and mealtimes.
- Support residents living with dementia and other complex care needs.
- Monitor and report changes in residents' health and wellbeing.
- Maintain accurate care documentation and follow individual care plans.
- Work collaboratively with nurses, senior carers and care home management.
- Adapt quickly to different care settings while maintaining professional standards.

What We Offer
- Competitive hourly rates of pay.
- Weekly pay.
- Day shifts, night shifts and weekend opportunities.
- Regular and ongoing work across the North East.
- Opportunities to pick up additional shifts at short notice.
- Support from our dedicated Newcastle-based recruitment team.
- A straightforward registration and compliance process.
- Opportunities to develop your experience across a variety of care environments.

Why Work With Tyne Trust Healthcare?

At Tyne Trust Healthcare, we value reliable, hardworking Healthcare Assistants who take pride in delivering exceptional care.

We work closely with established care providers throughout the North East and regularly receive requests for both planned and urgent staffing cover.

We are particularly interested in candidates who are dependable, responsive to last-minute bookings and committed to supporting our clients during weekends and periods of high demand.

In return, we offer a supportive team, regular communication and access to a wide variety of shifts.

Apply Today

If you're an experienced Healthcare Assistant who drives, is available for weekend work and can respond to last-minute shifts, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now with your updated CV to join Tyne Trust Healthcare.

Please ensure you meet all essential requirements before submitting your application.

title: Children's Residential Support Worker
description:
Children's Residential Support Worker

Sunderland
13.00 - 20.00 per hour
Zero Hour Contract

Pin Point Health & Social Care is recruiting experienced Children's Residential Support Workers to support young people aged 14-18 years within residential homes across Sunderland and the surrounding areas.

This is not a role for someone who wants to sit back and simply supervise. We're looking for proactive, engaging and energetic individuals who can build meaningful relationships with young people, encourage participation in activities, support independence, and create positive experiences throughout every shift.

The young people may have experienced trauma, adverse childhood experiences, emotional and behavioural difficulties (EBD), autism, learning disabilities, or other complex needs. You'll play a key role in providing a safe, stable, and nurturing environment while helping them develop confidence, resilience, and essential life skills.

The Role
- Supporting young people aged 14-18 with daily routines, education, appointments, and activities.
- Building positive relationships and acting as a consistent role model.
- Encouraging young people to engage in hobbies, community activities, education, and independent living skills.
- Supporting positive outcomes through a child-centred and therapeutic approach.
- Managing challenging behaviours in a calm and professional manner.
- Maintaining accurate records, reports, and handovers.
- Promoting safeguarding and the welfare of young people at all times.
- Working closely with residential staff and other professionals to provide the highest standard of care.

What We're Looking For
- At least 6 months' experience within a children's residential setting.
- Experience supporting young people with EBD, trauma, autism, or complex needs.
- A positive, proactive approach and a genuine passion for working with young people.
- Strong understanding of safeguarding and child-centred care.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Full UK driving licence preferred.
- Flexibility to work days, nights, weekends, and sleep-ins.

Why Join Pin Point Health & Social Care?
- Competitive hourly rates and weekly pay.
- Flexible work to fit around your availability.
- Regular ongoing shifts available.
- Dedicated consultant support.
- Training and development opportunities.

If you're an experienced Children's Residential Support Worker who enjoys building relationships, getting involved, and making a genuine difference to young people's lives, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today.

title: Young People Support Worker
description:
Young People Support Worker

We are seeking compassionate and motivated Support Workers to help young people in Durham build confidence, develop skills and move towards independence.

Position: Young People Support Worker and Night Young People Support Worker
Salary: £26,436 per annum plus excellent benefits
Location: Bishop Auckland Supported Accommodation Service and Tow Law Dispersed Accommodation Service, County Durham
Hours: Full time, 37.5 hours per week
Contract: Permanent, multiple vacancies
Closing date: 17 November 2026

About the Role

Join Depaul UK's supportive team and make a lasting difference to young people experiencing homelessness and other challenges.

We have opportunities for both Young People Support Workers and Night Young People Support Workers across our Bishop Auckland and Tow Law services.

In the day role, you will provide practical and emotional support to help young people develop independent living skills and work towards their goals. In the night role, you will help maintain a safe, welcoming and supportive environment overnight.

Your key responsibilities will include:

Building positive, trusting relationships and delivering tailored, person-centred support.

Completing risk and needs assessments and developing outcomes-based support plans.

Supporting young people to access education, training, employment and volunteering.

Delivering individual and group activities that build confidence, resilience and independence.

Working with colleagues and partner agencies to support wellbeing and safeguarding.

Helping young people settle into their accommodation and involving them in decisions about their support.

Maintaining a safe environment through regular checks and appropriate reporting.

Rotas may include unsocial hours and weekend working.

Please clearly state which role you are applying for and your preferred service location in your application or supporting statement.

About You

You will bring experience of working with young people or people who have experienced homelessness, alongside an understanding of needs relating to mental health and substance misuse.

You will also have:

Knowledge of risk assessments, support planning and safeguarding procedures.

Strong communication, relationship-building and collaborative working skills.

Good literacy, numeracy and IT skills.

A resilient, reflective approach and the ability to maintain professional boundaries.

A commitment to equality, diversity and treating everyone with dignity and respect.

About the Organisation

Since 1989, Depaul UK has supported young people facing homelessness. Through accommodation, prevention and support services, the charity helps thousands of young people each year recognise their potential and build brighter futures.

Benefits include tailored training, 26 days' annual leave rising with service, employer pension contributions up to 7%, family-friendly leave, an Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP access, a family cash health plan, discounts and death-in-service benefit.

Depaul UK welcomes applications from all backgrounds. Appropriate DBS checks apply where required, and a criminal record is not an automatic barrier to employment.

Other roles you may have experience of could include Youth Support Worker, Housing Support Worker, Supported Accommodation Worker, Homelessness Support Worker, Night Support Worker or Key Worker.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client - Not For Profit People.
